scenario: The Employee asks a question HR Assist can't answer without knowing how many days, which dates, when the request is submitted, and probation, is asked for it, and replies.

turns.content: Can I take leave next month?
Need more detail: how many days and which dates, when you're submitting, your remaining balance, whether you're in probation, and whether a critical delivery period applies.
5 days, Monday 16 to Friday 20 November 2026. I'm submitting the request today, and I've passed probation.

expected_outcome: Yes, you have given enough notice. Leave of more than 1 and up to 5 working days needs 10 working days' notice, approved by your line manager. Submitting on Tuesday 13 October for leave starting Monday 16 November gives 23 working days' notice, counting neither the submission date nor the first day of leave. The leave still has to be approved in PeopleHub before you take it, and if your team publishes a critical delivery period covering those dates, Head of Department approval is also needed.

scenario: The Employee asks a question HR Assist can't answer without knowing the type of absence and length of service, is asked for it, and replies.

turns.content: Will the company pay me while I'm off?
Depends on the type of absence (sickness, family leave, other leave), length of service/probation and eligibility; ask which.
It's sickness. I've worked here for 3 years and passed probation long ago.

expected_outcome: Yes. With 2 years' or more but less than 5 years' continuous service, company sick pay is 8 weeks at full pay, then 8 weeks at half pay, in any rolling 12-month period. Sick pay already paid in the previous 12 months is deducted from that entitlement. It includes Statutory Sick Pay rather than being paid on top of it, and it depends on following the sickness reporting procedure and providing the required evidence.

scenario: The Employee asks a question HR Assist can't answer without knowing the role designation and where the employee would work from, is asked for it, and replies.

turns.content: Can I work from home permanently?
Need role designation, whether you mean remote contract, and location (UK only); options are statutory flexible request or contractual change.
I'm in a hybrid role, and I'd work from my home in Manchester.

expected_outcome: You can ask to become remote-contracted. Changing your contractual place of work to your home is made as a statutory flexible-working request (or as part of a role change), and it needs approval from your Head of Department and People Operations. Your home is in the UK, so it is eligible. Request it normally at least 2 months before the change; if approved, it is recorded in a contract variation letter, and your salary doesn't change.

scenario: The Employee asks a question HR Assist can't answer without knowing what the expense is, the amount, date, purpose and receipt, is asked for it, and replies.

turns.content: Can I claim this expense?
Need what the expense is, amount, date incurred, business purpose, pre-approval and receipt.
A £35 taxi on 6 October 2026 from the station to a customer site, because I was carrying demo hardware. I have the itemised receipt.

expected_outcome: Yes. A taxi is reimbursable up to £50 per journey when you are carrying heavy or valuable equipment, so £35 is within the limit. Attach the itemised receipt and submit the claim within 30 calendar days of 6 October 2026, that is by 5 November 2026.

scenario: The Employee asks a question HR Assist can't answer without knowing which kind of parental leave, employee status and the child's age, is asked for it, and replies.

turns.content: Am I eligible for parental leave?
Which leave: unpaid parental leave, shared parental, paternity, maternity/adoption? Also employee status and parental responsibility/child's age.
I mean unpaid parental leave. I'm an employee, and my daughter is 4.

expected_outcome: Yes. Unpaid parental leave has been a day-one right since 6 April 2026. With parental responsibility, you can take up to 18 weeks for your daughter before her 18th birthday, at most 4 weeks in any year, in whole weeks, giving 21 days' notice of the start and end dates. Northstar can postpone it by up to 6 months if the business would be unduly disrupted.

scenario: The Employee asks a question HR Assist can't answer without knowing whether it is notice of resignation or of a leave request, and the grade, is asked for it, and replies.

turns.content: How much notice do I need to give?
Notice for what — resigning (depends on grade/probation) or a leave request (depends on length)?
I mean resigning. I've passed probation, and I'm grade G4.

expected_outcome: You need to give 2 months' notice: that is the contractual notice for grades G4 and G5 after probation. Your individual employment contract prevails if it says something different.

scenario: The Employee asks a question HR Assist can't answer without knowing the purpose of the trip and the destination, is asked for it, and replies.

turns.content: Can I take my work laptop abroad?
Need purpose (business trip, Work From Abroad, or holiday), destination and data you'll access.
It's a holiday in Spain, and I'd like to work for 3 days while I'm there. I've passed probation.

expected_outcome: Working while abroad needs an approved Work From Abroad request. Submit it in PeopleHub at least 4 weeks before you travel; it needs approval from your line manager, People Operations and IT Security. The 3 days count towards the limit of 10 working days in any rolling 12 months. You must be available for UK core hours (10:00 to 16:00 UK time), and you must not access Restricted information without written CISO approval.
